title: Node Detail

links.title: This node in the PE console

panels.title: Firing Alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing for this node right now, via the ALERTS series. Usually the reason somebody arrived here, so it is the first thing on the board.

panels.title: Run Failed
panels.description: Whether this node's most recent run failed. This is usually the reason somebody arrived here, so it is the first thing on the board.

panels.title: Since Last Report
panels.description: A node that has stopped reporting shows its last known state indefinitely, so read every other tile here against this one.

panels.title: Noop Mode
panels.description: Running in noop, so Puppet is reporting what it would change and changing nothing. A node in noop looks converged and is not.

panels.title: Reboot Required
panels.description: Puppet has applied something that needs a reboot to take effect. Scheduling information rather than a fault.

panels.title: App Restart
panels.description: A service on this node needs restarting to finish applying what Puppet has already done.

panels.title: Security Exposure

targets.expr: (((time() - max by (node) (last_over_time(timestamp(puppet_patching_data{type="security",node="$node",alias=~"$nodepe"} == 0)[30d:1h]))) and on(node) (max by (node) (puppet_patching_data{type="security",node="$node",alias=~"$nodepe"}) > 0)) or ((max by (node) (puppet_patching_data{type="security",node="$node",alias=~"$nodepe"}) > 0) * 0 + (30 * 86400)))

panels.description: How long this node has carried at least one outstanding security patch, counted from the last time it read zero. Capped at 30 days, which is how far back the query looks. Empty is the answer you want and means nothing is outstanding.

panels.title: Patching Blocked
panels.description: Something is stopping this node patching. PDCTNG Patching has the fleet view of why.

panels.title: Overdue By
panels.description: How late this node is against **its own** schedule: time since its last report, minus its `runinterval`, minus its `splaylimit`. Zero means it is not due yet. Read it instead of Since Last Report above when deciding whether silence is a fault -- a node on a 30-minute interval with 30 minutes of splay is entitled to be an hour behind, and that tile has to use one fixed threshold for every node on the estate.

panels.title: Catalogue Lag
panels.description: How far ahead of its own catalogue this node's last report is. On a healthy node that is the length of the run, a handful of seconds. Hours or days mean the agent applied a cached catalogue because it could not reach a compiler, so the node is enforcing what it was told to do the last time anybody asked. Says nothing about a node that has stopped reporting altogether: read Since Last Report and Overdue By for that.

panels.title: Facts Lag
panels.description: How far ahead of its own facts this node's last report is. Facts are submitted at the start of a run and the report at the end, so a few seconds is the healthy reading and facts always precede their report. A large number means the facts upload is failing while runs continue, so the primary is classifying this node on a picture that has stopped moving.

panels.title: Run Cut Short
panels.description: Whether the last run's transaction failed to complete, which is not the same as a run that failed. A failed run applied what it could and reported it; a transaction that never completed was interrupted, so the counts on this board describe a run that stopped partway rather than a run that finished badly.

panels.title: Patches Outstanding
panels.description: Outstanding updates by kind. Security patches are the ones with a deadline attached.

panels.title: CIS Scores
panels.description: This node's compliance score, before and after agreed exceptions. Absent means it has never been scanned; a score here can still be months old, which PDCTNG CIS Compliance will tell you.

panels.title: CIS Scan Age
panels.description: How long since this node was scanned, and against which benchmark and profile. The score beside this is only as current as this number: a scanner that stopped leaves the last score sitting there looking healthy. The board used to send you to PDCTNG CIS Compliance to find this out about your own node.

panels.title: What The Exceptions Are Worth
panels.description: Percentage points this node gains from agreed exceptions: the adjusted score less the base score. Both numbers are on the gauge beside this and the gap between them is the thing nobody could read off it. Zero means the exceptions this node carries are buying it nothing, which is a withdrawal candidate; PDCTNG CIS Rules shows the same question fleet-wide.

panels.title: What did the last run do?
Failed Events
panels.description: Resources that failed to apply in the last run. Zero here with Run Failed showing yes means the run died before it applied anything, usually a compile or a connection problem.

panels.title: Changes
panels.description: Resources this node changed in its last run. Steady non-zero every run is a node fighting something.

panels.title: Successful Events
panels.description: Resources that applied cleanly.

panels.title: Total Events
panels.description: Every event in the last report, the denominator for the two tiles before it.

panels.title: Resources
panels.description: Resources in this node's catalogue. A number that grows steadily over months is the catalogue getting more expensive to compile.

panels.title: Run Duration
panels.description: How long the last run took end to end.

panels.title: Where the Run Spent Its Time
panels.description: The last run broken down by resource type. One type dominating is where to look when a run gets slow.

panels.title: Resources By Status

targets.expr: puppet_report_resources{node="$node",alias=~"$nodepe",name!~"(Total|Out of sync)"} > -1 or label_replace(puppet_report_resources{node="$node",alias=~"$nodepe",name="Total"} - on(node) puppet_report_resources{node="$node",alias=~"$nodepe",name="Out of sync"}, "name", "Unchanged", "", "")

panels.description: What the last run did to this node's resources. Corrective change is counted inside Changed, so the two are not additive. Unchanged is computed rather than reported: Puppet's report metrics have no key for it, so it is the catalogue size less the resources that were out of sync, which is how the PE console arrives at the same number.

panels.title: Is the machine itself the problem?
Load Per Core
panels.description: One-minute load average divided by cores. Needs node_exporter on this node, and matches it to the certname by name, so it is empty where the certname is not the FQDN. Full detail is on PDCTNG Node Metrics, linked at the top.

panels.title: Memory Used
panels.description: One minus MemAvailable over total, not MemFree, which reads near zero on any host with a page cache and means nothing.

panels.title: Fullest Filesystem
panels.description: The fullest real filesystem on this host. A node whose disk is full fails its runs for reasons no Puppet metric explains.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since boot. Under an hour explains a missed run, a cold cache, and a report that arrived late, all at once.

panels.title: Has it always been like this?
Run Duration Over Time
panels.description: Total run time against config retrieval, which is the compile. Total climbing while config retrieval stays flat is this node getting slower; both climbing is the server.

panels.title: Resources By Status Over Time
panels.description: Whether this node has always looked like this. A step change lines up against the deploy markers. Total and Out of sync are left out for the same reasons Resources By Status leaves them out: the catalogue size is the Resources tile above, and Out of sync counts the same resources Changed and Failed already do.

panels.title: Resource Application Time
panels.description: Time per resource type over the window. A row that darkens is a resource type getting more expensive on this node specifically.

description: One node: is it healthy, what did its last run do, and has it always been like this.
